tools.name: diagnose_crash
tools.description: Diagnose a GPU/ML training crash (CUDA OOM, NCCL timeout, Xid fault, NaN loss, checkpoint corruption, etc.) and get the root cause plus an escalating fix (primary → fallback → emergency). Provide ONE of: `logs` (paste), `file` (path to a log), or `dir` (folder to scan for the newest *.err/*.log). Uses the Denpex cloud by default, or runs fully offline with DENPEX_LOCAL=1.

logs.description: Paste the crash log or stderr. Terse machine events such as Xid 79 are accepted.

file.description: Path to a log file to read from disk.

dir.description: Directory to scan for the newest *.err / *.log / *.out / *.txt.

jobName.description: Optional job or run name (saved to history).

runtimeHours.description: Hours the job ran before crashing (enables a $ cost estimate).

telemetry.description: Hardware telemetry captured from the failing node. Keys the engine reads: `dmesg` (output of `dmesg -T`), `nvidia_smi` (`nvidia-smi -q`), `ibstat`. Sending these turns an ambiguous NCCL timeout into a specific Xid/ECC verdict, and, just as importantly, lets the engine EXONERATE the GPU when the counters are clean.

codeContext.description: Relevant source files as { path: contents }. Only send real files you read, the engine never fabricates code context, and neither should you.

topologyMap.description: Rank → node placement as { nodeName: [rank...] }, e.g. from the launcher. Lets the engine map a failing rank to a physical node and GPU.

operatorAnswers.description: Answers from a previous diagnose_crash result. Send the full answer history with the same original logs. Selecting an ACTION asks Denpex for that evidence; it is not treated as the result of the check.

refinementToken.description: Anonymous-only capability returned by the prior diagnosis. Normally cached automatically in this MCP process; pass it explicitly after a process restart.

tools.name: inspect_gpu_artifact
tools.description: Read-only local inspection of PyTorch Flight Recorder JSON rank dumps, CUDA memory snapshot JSON, Nsight SQLite, checkpoint candidates or aligned rank timing JSON. Requires Python 3; uses no network and never executes pickle or changes checkpoints. Pass the resulting JSON to diagnose_crash as logs to review or save it using your normal Denpex configuration.

path.description: Local artifact file or checkpoint root directory.

tools.name: lookup_failure
tools.description: Search Denpex's bundled 721-class failure encyclopedia by error code, keyword, or symptom (e.g. 'Xid 79', 'NCCL timeout', 'loss is NaN', 'CUDA out of memory'). Returns the most relevant known failures with their fixes. Works fully offline and costs no quota. Use `diagnose_crash` instead when you have a full crash log.

query.description: Error code, message, or symptom to look up.

tools.name: analyze_cascade
tools.description: Analyze a multi-rank distributed-training failure: find the rank that failed FIRST (the others usually just time out waiting on it) and route any GPU Xid faults to the correct node action (reset / reboot / RMA). Runs offline and instantly, provide the gathered per-rank logs via `logs`, `file`, or `dir`.

file.description: Path to a log file to read.

dir.description: Directory to scan for the newest log file.

tools.name: check_quota
tools.description: Show your Denpex plan, allowance tier, and diagnoses left today.

tools.name: ask_followup
tools.description: Ask the Denpex diagnostician a follow-up question about a crash, clarify the fix, explore an alternative, or dig deeper. Pass the original `logs` and your `question`; pass back the `conversationId` from a previous reply to continue the thread. Requires the Team plan or an active trial.

logs.description: The original crash logs the question is about.

conversationId.description: From a previous reply, to continue the same thread.

history.description: Prior turns of this conversation, oldest first.

tools.name: check_versions
tools.description: Scan logs (or an environment dump like `pip list` / `nvidia-smi`) for CUDA / PyTorch / cuDNN / NCCL / driver versions that are known to be incompatible or buggy together, and get the recommended pin. Requires the Team plan or an active trial.

logs.description: Paste logs or an environment dump.

file.description: Path to a log / environment file.

dir.description: Directory to scan for the newest log file.

tools.name: list_incidents
tools.description: List the GPU/training incidents Denpex's always-on monitor caught and auto-escalated on your fleet, failure type, cluster, escalation level, and the fix it applied. Requires the Scale plan or higher.

tools.name: recent_diagnoses
tools.description: Show your most recent Denpex diagnoses, job name, failure type, confidence, and the fix, so you can recall what a prior crash was and how it was resolved.

tools.name: submit_fix_outcome
tools.description: Report back whether a Denpex fix actually resolved the failure. Call this after you apply a fix from `diagnose_crash` and observe the result, it is the ONLY way the engine learns, and it directly improves the next diagnosis of this failure class for you and everyone else. Pass the `diagnosisId` printed at the bottom of the diagnosis. If the fix did not work, say what actually happened in `note` (and `newFix` if you found the real one), a specific negative is worth more than a vague positive.

diagnosisId.description: The `diagnosisId` from the diagnosis you acted on.

outcome.description: `worked` = the failure is resolved and the job is progressing. `did_not_work` = it recurred or the fix did not apply.

note.description: What actually happened. On a `did_not_work`, this is the most valuable field in the call, say what the log showed after the fix.

newFix.description: If you found the real fix, what was it?

tools.name: launch_gate
tools.description: Evaluate the EXACT allocation a scheduler is about to hand out, these nodes, these GPU indices, against what Denpex knows about them: quarantined or repeat-offender cards, split driver versions inside one collective, software combinations that have crashed and never completed, degraded fabric links, an incomplete distributed checkpoint, storage about to hit ENOSPC. Returns GO / GO_WITH_WARNING / REQUIRE_APPROVAL / BLOCK with the evidence for each. Advisory unless `enforce` is true. IMPORTANT: a check Denpex could not evaluate is reported as unknown, never as a pass, read `evidenceCoverage` before treating a GO as an all-clear.

gpus.description: Every GPU the scheduler proposes to allocate.

stack.description: Software the job will run with. Omitting it makes the known-bad-cohort check report unknown.

enforce.description: Apply the verdict. Default false, advisory only.

tools.name: preflight_check
tools.description: Answer 'is this cluster safe to launch on?' BEFORE you burn GPU-hours on a job that will die in the first ten minutes. Feed it the health artifacts from the nodes you are about to use, `nvidia-smi -q`, `ibstat`, `nvidia-smi topo -m`, `dmesg -T`, and it returns the critical blockers (dead links, missing GPUs, non-NVLink topology, driver mismatch) that would take the run down. Scale+ feature.

logs.description: Paste the health artifacts (nvidia-smi -q, ibstat, nvidia-smi topo -m, dmesg -T).

file.description: Path to a file containing them.

dir.description: Directory to scan for the newest artifact file.

tools.name: compare_runs
tools.description: 'It worked yesterday.' Give it the logs from the run that worked and the run that failed, and it isolates what actually changed between them instead of re-diagnosing the failure from scratch. Use this whenever a previously-green job starts failing.

successLogs.description: Logs from the run that worked.

failLogs.description: Logs from the run that failed.

tools.name: diff_environments
tools.description: Diff the SOFTWARE environment between a good run and a bad one, torch / CUDA / NCCL / driver / flash-attn versions, env vars, and flag combinations known to be broken. Feed it `pip freeze`, `nvidia-smi`, `env` output (or the whole job log; it extracts what it needs). Use this when `compare_runs` points at a version change, or when a job breaks after an image rebuild.

goodRun.description: Artifacts from the last good run (pip freeze / nvidia-smi / env, or the full log).

badRun.description: The same artifacts from the failing run.

failureLogs.description: Optional: the failure output itself, for fingerprinting.

tools.name: validate_checkpoint
tools.description: Inspect directory listings, checksum output and load errors for signs of checkpoint corruption. Supplied metadata does not verify full shard coverage, compatible optimizer state or successful workload recovery. Validate actual loading and intended progress before resuming.

directoryListing.description: Output of `ls -la` (or `ls -la --time-style=full-iso`) on the checkpoint directory.

sha256Output.description: Output of `sha256sum -c MANIFEST.sha256`, if you keep a manifest.

loadErrors.description: Any error output from trying to load a checkpoint.

failureType.description: The diagnosed failure type, if you have one, it sharpens the verdict.

tools.name: node_health
tools.description: Score the health of every node Denpex is monitoring in your fleet, worst first. Use it to answer 'which nodes should I exclude from this job?' before scheduling, or 'what else is degrading?' after an incident. Scale+ feature; requires the Denpex agent to be reporting.

tools.name: predict_failures
tools.description: List the predictive risk scores Denpex has computed for your fleet, nodes whose counters are trending toward a failure that has not happened yet (rising correctable ECC, row-remap pressure, PCIe replays, thermal drift). Use it to drain a node on your schedule instead of the cluster's. Scale+ feature.
